electrical_safety.name: electrical_safety
electrical_safety.description: Electrical safety refers to the identification, prevention, and control of hazards related to the use and maintenance of electrical systems and equipment in the workplace. It encompasses safe work practices, hazard recognition, and compliance with regulations to prevent electrical injuries, fires, and equipment damage. Observations in this category often involve unsafe wiring, improper use of electrical tools, or lack of protective measures.
examples: Observed missing lockout tag on electrical panel.
Extension cords running across walkways without protection.
Employee using damaged power tool with exposed wires.
No warning signage near high voltage area.
Routine electrical safety inspection completed.

arc_flash.name: arc_flash
arc_flash.description: Arc flash refers to a dangerous release of energy caused by an electrical arc, resulting in intense heat, light, and pressure that can cause severe injuries or fatalities. In HSE, this category covers incidents, near misses, or hazards where workers are exposed to arc flash risks, often during maintenance or operation of electrical equipment. Observations may include inadequate PPE, improper procedures, or lack of arc flash labeling.
examples: Worker entered switchgear room without arc flash PPE.
Arc flash label missing on main distribution panel.
Near miss: arc flash occurred during breaker maintenance.
Observed burn marks from previous arc flash event.
No arc flash boundary marked on electrical cabinet.

fire_risk.name: fire_risk
fire_risk.description: Fire risk involves the potential for ignition, spread, and harm from fire due to electrical faults, flammable materials, or unsafe practices. In HSE, this category includes observations of conditions or behaviors that could lead to fire, such as overloaded circuits, accumulation of combustible dust, or blocked fire exits. It is critical for preventing property damage, injuries, and environmental harm.
examples: Overloaded power strip found behind server rack.
Flammable materials stored near electrical panel.
Fire extinguisher blocked by equipment.
Accumulation of dust in electrical room.
Unattended soldering iron left plugged in.

short_circuit.name: short_circuit
short_circuit.description: Short circuit refers to an unintended connection between two points in an electrical circuit, causing excessive current flow and potential equipment damage, fire, or injury. In HSE, this category covers incidents, hazards, or near misses involving short circuits, often due to faulty wiring, damaged insulation, or improper repairs. Observations may include tripped breakers, burnt smells, or visible sparks.
examples: Breaker tripped due to short circuit in lighting panel.
Burnt smell detected near motor control center.
Observed sparks from junction box during operation.
Short circuit caused power outage in production area.
Damaged cable insulation led to short circuit.

wiring_fault.name: wiring_fault
wiring_fault.description: Wiring fault refers to defects or errors in electrical wiring, such as loose connections, incorrect wiring, or damaged cables, which can lead to equipment failure, fire, or electric shock. In HSE, this category includes observations of improper installations, exposed conductors, or signs of wear and tear in wiring systems. Timely identification is crucial for preventing incidents.
examples: Loose wire connection found in control panel.
Incorrectly wired outlet discovered during inspection.
Damaged insulation on power cable near machine.
Exposed conductor observed in ceiling wiring.
Wiring fault caused intermittent equipment shutdown.

equipment_failure.name: equipment_failure
equipment_failure.description: Equipment failure refers to the malfunction or breakdown of electrical or mechanical devices, which can create safety hazards, disrupt operations, or lead to secondary incidents. In HSE, this category includes reports of failed machinery, tripped systems, or non-functional safety devices, often requiring immediate maintenance or shutdown.
examples: Main generator failed during routine operation.
Emergency stop button not functioning on conveyor.
Pump motor overheated and shut down unexpectedly.
Fire alarm panel displayed equipment fault code.
Lighting system failure in warehouse area.

overload.name: overload
overload.description: Overload refers to a condition where electrical circuits or equipment are subjected to currents or loads beyond their rated capacity, increasing the risk of overheating, fire, or equipment damage. In HSE, this category includes observations of overloaded outlets, excessive use of extension cords, or machinery running above safe limits.
examples: Multiple heaters plugged into single outlet caused overload.
Observed tripped breaker due to circuit overload.
Extension cord used to power several high-wattage devices.
Motor running above rated load for extended period.
Overload warning displayed on control panel.

ground_fault.name: ground_fault
ground_fault.description: Ground fault refers to an unintentional electrical path between a power source and the ground, which can result in electric shock, equipment damage, or fire. In HSE, this category includes incidents or hazards where faulty insulation, damaged equipment, or moisture leads to current leakage to ground.
examples: Ground fault detected on portable generator.
Moisture in panel caused ground fault trip.
Worker received mild shock due to ground fault in tool.
Ground fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) activated in restroom.
Insulation failure led to ground fault in lighting system.

exposed_wiring.name: exposed_wiring
exposed_wiring.description: Exposed wiring refers to electrical conductors that are not properly insulated or covered, posing risks of electric shock, short circuit, or fire. In HSE, this category includes observations of bare wires, damaged cable sheaths, or temporary wiring left unprotected in work areas.
examples: Exposed wires found near loading dock.
Temporary wiring left uncovered in hallway.
Damaged cable sheath exposing conductors.
Bare wires hanging from ceiling light fixture.
Observed uninsulated wiring in maintenance area.

power_outage.name: power_outage
power_outage.description: Power outage refers to the loss of electrical supply to a facility or area, which can disrupt operations, compromise safety systems, and create hazards for workers. In HSE, this category includes both planned and unplanned outages, as well as their impacts on critical equipment and emergency procedures.
examples: Unplanned power outage halted production line.
Backup generator activated during power failure.
Emergency lighting failed to operate during blackout.
Power outage affected fire alarm system.
Planned power shutdown for maintenance announced.

shock_hazard.name: shock_hazard
shock_hazard.description: Shock hazard refers to the risk of electric shock due to contact with live electrical parts, faulty equipment, or improper grounding. In HSE, this category includes observations of unsafe conditions where workers could be exposed to electrical current, such as missing covers, wet environments, or damaged tools.
examples: Missing cover on live electrical panel presents shock hazard.
Wet floor near power outlet increases shock risk.
Damaged extension cord exposes workers to electric shock.
Observed worker using tool with frayed power cord.
Improperly grounded equipment identified as shock hazard.
